title: From Entity Mentions to Tone: An LLM-Based Pipeline for Media Bias Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2608.17454v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper presents a pipeline for analyzing media bias and framing in online news. The pipeline groups articles into topics and events, adds named-entity and sentiment annotations, and compares news sources through people mentions, source-level tone, and event-level coverage patterns. We apply it to 8,358 Albanian news articles collected from GDELT and compare the resulting annotations with GDELT's automated annotations. The results show moderate agreement for sentiment and entity extraction, as well as additional person-entity pairs that can potentially support the bias analysis. We compare two annotation prompts and find that stricter sentiment-validation rules remove label-score inconsistencies but increase execution time and reduce annotation coverage. translated_title: 从实体提及到语气：一种基于大语言模型的媒体偏见分析流水线
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一种用于分析在线新闻中媒体偏见和框架效应的流水线。该流水线将文章按主题和事件分组，添加命名实体和情感标注，并通过人物提及、来源级别语气和事件级别的报道模式来比较新闻来源。我们将其应用于从GDELT收集的8,358篇阿尔巴尼亚语新闻文章，并将生成的标注与GDELT的自动标注进行比较。结果显示，在情感和实体提取方面存在中等程度的一致性，以及额外的可能支持偏见分析的人物-实体对。我们比较了两种标注提示，发现更严格的情感验证规则消除了标签-分数不一致性，但增加了执行时间并减少了标注覆盖范围。基于这些结果，在后续分析中使用了更简单的提示。我们提供了来源级别框架概况、人物级别语气差异的示例分析。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于大语言模型的流水线，用于自动分析新闻中的媒体偏见和框架，并通过比较不同提示策略优化了情感标注的准确性与覆盖范围。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an LLM-based pipeline for automated media bias and framing analysis in news, optimizing sentiment annotation accuracy and coverage through prompt strategy comparison.
